human_relevance_statement: A large body of work has demonstrated that pet dogs with spontaneous diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) represent a relevant large-animal model of the human disease, with numerous genetic changes and pathway aberrations shared across both species. Using an adaptive trial design, small-molecule immune modulators were combined with anti-CD20 and low dose doxorubicin to identify promising therapeutic regimens and associated biomarkers of activity. In doing so, this clinical trial created a framework within which to rapidly optimize novel treatment strategies for DLBCL prior to evaluation in human patients, with the goal of improving clinical translation.
relevant_experimental_therapeutic_interv: anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody;doxorubicin;RV1001 (PI3K-delta inhibitor);KPT-9274 (NAMPT/PAK4 inhibitor);TAK-981 (SUMO-activating enzyme inhibitor)
relevant_human_pathways: PI3K-delta signaling;NAD+ biosynthesis (NAMPT salvage pathway);PAK4 signaling;protein SUMOylation;B-cell receptor signaling
